Aloof

/uh-LOOF/ - rhymes with roof · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Aloof means reserved, distant.

Even after three seasons with the troupe, the understudy remained aloof, warming up alone in the wings while the cast traded jokes onstage.

Worked Example

Everyone at the reunion assumed the visiting cousin thought himself above them: he kept to the porch rail, answered warmly enough when approached, but never once crossed the lawn to join a conversation. He wasn't rude—just aloof, holding the whole gathering at arm's length.

Aloof is more precise than 'shy' or 'unfriendly' because it describes chosen distance without open hostility—an aloof person stays apart and lets others do the approaching, which can read as coolness even when no offense is meant.

How Aloof Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

standoffish

standoffish: informal; the coolness is felt by others as mild rudeness

withdrawn

withdrawn: pulled inward, often from grief or exhaustion rather than preference

Antonyms

approachable

approachable: easy to walk up to and talk with

sociable

sociable: actively seeks out company

How Strong Is It? — standoffish → aloof → unapproachable

standoffish vs. aloof

standoffish vs. aloof: Standoffish is the milder, everyday word—a standoffish clerk skips the small talk but still serves you cheerfully enough.

unapproachable vs. aloof

unapproachable vs. aloof: Unapproachable goes further than standoffish—an unapproachable director has a wall around her that nobody on staff will even try to cross.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of aloof.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — a-

Prefix — a-: on, toward (an old nautical prefix)

Root — loof

Root — loof: the windward side of a ship (from Dutch loef)

Put it together

Put it together: A- (on, toward) + loof (the windward side of a ship, from Dutch loef) = steering to windward, keeping clear. Sailors held a ship 'aloof' to keep her safely apart from a dangerous shore; by the 1600s the word had drifted from seamanship to people who keep themselves apart.

Why there's no relative to spot

Why there's no relative to spot: The loof in aloof survives almost nowhere else—English keeps it only in the sailing term luff, the windward edge of a sail—so aloof stands alone, a fossil of old deck commands.

Strength Check

Word Choice

neutral, slightly formal

Aloof describes cool, self-chosen distance without open rudeness—the aloof stay composed and apart, letting others approach first. Keep it separate from two unit-mates: bashful people hang back out of blushing embarrassment, and diffident people out of self-doubt; the aloof hang back because they prefer the distance.
